description: Make the build-release.sh AC4 soft-check hermetic: run the init smoke in a throwaway mktemp -d cwd with --no-tmux so it never mutates the repo working tree or spawns a tmux session / claude agent.
docsConsultedRationale: No external library touched: a bash build script change (mktemp, cd, --no-tmux flag already supported by the cam binary) plus a static-assertion bun test. No npm API exercised.

userStories.title: Run the build-release AC4 soft-check in a hermetic tmpdir with --no-tmux
userStories.description: As the release build, I need the init soft-check to validate the binary without mutating the repo working tree or spawning tmux, so a build never clobbers versioned files or leaves live claude processes (it bit the operator twice).
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/build-release.sh AC4 soft-check creates a throwaway directory via mktemp -d and runs the binary with that directory as cwd, so any template install lands in the tmpdir, never the repo.

The soft-check invokes the binary as `init --no-tmux --existing --issue-system none` (NOT plain `init`) with stdin redirected from /dev/null, so neither the tmux split, the setup agent, nor the interactive setup wizard (collectSetupAnswers) is ever reached: --existing skips the project-mode prompt and avoids the description prompt, --issue-system none skips the issue prompt, --no-tmux skips the tmux+agent spawn, and </dev/null prevents any residual readline from blocking.
The binary is referenced by an absolute path (e.g. ${REPO_ROOT}/${BIN}) so the cd into the tmpdir does not break resolution.
CAM_CONFIG_PATH still points at a temp config so the operator's real config is untouched.
The tmpdir is removed (rm -rf) after the soft-check.
Non-zero exit from the soft-check is still logged but does NOT abort the build (machines without claude installed are tolerated, preserving the existing AC4 semantics).
After running ./scripts/build-release.sh (no --install), `git status --porcelain` is empty (the build does not touch the working tree).
`bash -n scripts/build-release.sh` passes (syntax check).
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: File: scripts/build-release.sh (the AC4 block at lines ~92-107). The cam binary already chains init -> runInit (read-only machine validation) -> runSetup({cwd, noTmux}); runSetup writes project.toml + copyTemplates relative to cwd and, unless noTmux, spawns tmux + a setup agent (src/commands/setup.ts). runSetup also runs collectSetupAnswers (src/commands/setup.ts ~96): it prompts for project mode, issue system, and (for 'new') a description UNLESS pre-filled by flags. So the hermetic invocation must be `init --no-tmux --existing --issue-system none </dev/null` (--existing => projectMode set + no description needed; --issue-system none => no issue prompt; --no-tmux => no tmux/agent). cd into a mktemp -d isolates the file writes. BIN is currently the relative path dist/cam-darwin-arm64; compute an absolute path for the subshell. Canonical rule: lessons.md 2026-06-06 entry ('build smoke must never run a mutating command against the repo; use a temp cwd'). Do NOT change the compile/codesign/version steps.

userStories.title: Static guard test: build-release smoke is hermetic
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need a test that fails if the build-release soft-check ever regresses to mutating the repo, so the hermetic invariant is enforced in CI.
acceptanceCriteria: A new test file test/build-release-smoke.test.ts reads scripts/build-release.sh and asserts the soft-check is hermetic.

It asserts the script contains an `mktemp -d` for the smoke and that the binary `init` invocation carries ALL of: `--no-tmux`, `--existing`, and `--issue-system none` (the non-interactive + no-tmux flag set), plus a `</dev/null` stdin redirect.

It asserts the only `init` invocation of the binary in the script (a) is preceded by a cd into the smoke tmpdir (or equivalent), (b) carries --no-tmux, and (c) uses an absolute binary path (not a bare relative dist/cam-darwin-arm64 resolved from inside the tmpdir). All three together close the regression surface.
The test mirrors the static-source-assertion style of test/no-permission-mode-flag.test.ts (read the file, assert substrings/patterns; no compiled binary needed; resilient to minor whitespace).
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: File: test/build-release-smoke.test.ts (new). Read scripts/build-release.sh via Bun.file. Assert: includes 'mktemp -d', includes 'init --no-tmux', and that the only `${BIN...} init` / `cam init`-style invocation is the hermetic one (guard against a future plain `init` against REPO_ROOT). Keep assertions resilient to minor formatting (match on the meaningful tokens, not exact whitespace).

userStories.title: Operator validation: real build leaves a clean working tree
userStories.description: As the operator, I need to run the real release build and confirm it no longer mutates the repo or spawns tmux, since that runtime side effect is exactly what a static test cannot prove.
acceptanceCriteria: On the operator machine (claude installed + logged in, so the setup path is actually exercised), run ./scripts/build-release.sh (no --install) from a clean working tree.

After the build, `git status --porcelain` is empty: none of .claude/agents/*.md, .claude/commands/*.md, scripts/cam/project.toml, scripts/cam/journal.md, scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md, or .claude/.cam-orchestrator-prompt.txt were modified.
No tmux session named cam-setup exists afterward (tmux -L cam list-sessions shows none) and no orphan claude / .cam-setup-menu.sh process was left running.
Operator records the before/after `git status` as evidence.
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Real-build verification of the side-effect removal. Needs a real machine with claude logged in so runSetup's claude check passes and the (now hermetic) template install + skipped-tmux path actually runs. Evidence: git status before == after == clean. Reference: lessons.md 2026-06-06; the CAM-16 US-003 ceremony log is where this side effect was last observed (10 files clobbered + cam-setup session).
